_source: DOSBox's own OPL2, driven directly via ports 0x388/0x389 from a bare DOS prompt with no program running, so nothing else could touch the chip. One test per key-on: channel 0, FM mode, feedback 0, modulator (slot 0) silenced with TL=63 so the carrier (slot 3) is heard alone as a clean sine. fnum=0x244, block=4 => 440 Hz, which the capture confirms (measured 435-448 Hz across the six tests). Audio captured with DOSBox's own ZMBV video capture (bridge config mute=false, headless=false), audio track extracted with ffmpeg, envelope measured in 2 ms RMS frames.
_measurement: attack_ms is the 10%->90% rise of the RMS envelope; decay_ms is peak->10%. Resolution is 2 ms, so the fastest rates are at the floor and are recorded but not used for fitting.

_derived.rate_law: time scales by 2^(-internal_rate/4); measured attack ratio rate16:rate32 = 130/8 = 16.25 against a predicted 16
